title: Grade 4 CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — 1.2 Thoughts and feelings

pages.lesson:
PAGE 1: Overview

OVERVIEW
========

Thoughts are what you think, and feelings are what you feel inside. In this sub-strand you will name good thoughts, learn why joy matters, and read Ephesians 4:26 and Philippians 4:4. You will practise ways to cope with anger and sadness without hurting yourself or other people.

## Strand 1.0: Creation
Sub-strand 1.2: Thoughts and feelings
Suggested lessons: 3

## Learning outcomes
By the end of the sub-strand, the learner should be able to:
a) identify good thoughts and feelings
b) explain the importance of being joyful
c) list lessons learnt from Ephesians 4:26
d) apply the lessons learnt to cope with emotions in day-to-day life

## Key inquiry questions
1. How do you control your thoughts and feelings?
2. How do you cope with anger or sadness?

## Core competencies
• Learning to learn: the skill of sharing experiences is nurtured as learners tell each other how they cope with emotions such as anger or sadness.

## Values
• Love: is nurtured as learners role-play forgiving others when wronged.

## Pertinent and contemporary issues
• Social cohesion is nurtured as learners list good thoughts such as sharing with others, helping parents, being happy, being thankful and respecting others.

## Links to other learning areas
• Creative Arts: creative skills are applied as learners sing, dance, draw and colour pictures of faces depicting various emotions.
• English: speaking skills are applied as learners recite Bible verses.

## Source
• KICD Grade 4 Christian Religious Education Curriculum Design (Revised 2024) — Strand 1.0 Creation, Sub-strand 1.2 Thoughts and feelings
• Ephesians 4:26; Philippians 4:4

PAGE 2: Lesson 1: Good thoughts and good feelings

LESSON 1: GOOD THOUGHTS AND GOOD FEELINGS
=========================================

## What you will learn
• Identify good thoughts and good feelings.
• Give examples of good thoughts such as sharing, helping, thankfulness and respect.

Curriculum outcomes: a) identify good thoughts and feelings

## Introduction
Before you speak or act, a thought passes through your mind. A kind thought can lead to a kind action. A bitter thought can lead to a hurtful one. God cares about what we think and what we feel.

## Notes
A thought is an idea in your mind. A feeling is what you experience inside, such as joy, sadness, fear or anger. You cannot see a thought, but you can see what it leads you to do.

### Good thoughts
Good thoughts please God and help people live together in peace. Examples from daily life are:

- Sharing with others, such as sharing a pencil or lunch
- Helping parents with work at home
- Being happy for a classmate who does well
- Being thankful for food, family and school
- Respecting others by using polite words

A good thought asks, "Will this help someone? Is this true? Is this kind?" If the answer is yes, the thought is worth keeping.

### Good feelings
Good feelings include joy, peace, love, thankfulness and hope. They do not mean you never feel sad. They mean your heart is learning to choose what is right. When you think about helping your mother, you may feel glad. When you forgive a friend, you may feel peace.

### Controlling thoughts
You control thoughts by noticing them. If a thought says, "Take her rubber and hide it," you can stop and replace it with, "I will ask to borrow it." Singing a song about good thoughts, praying, and talking to a parent or teacher helps. Drawing a smiling face and a kind face reminds you that feelings can be seen on the outside.

Social cohesion grows when a class lists good thoughts together. Sharing, helping, thankfulness and respect keep people close.

## Key words
• thought — an idea in the mind
• feeling — what a person experiences inside, such as joy or sadness
• thankful — glad for what you have received

## Activity: List good thoughts and sing
You will need: Manila paper, Pencils, Digital device if the teacher provides one
1. Sing a song related to good thoughts and feelings.
2. In groups, list good thoughts such as sharing, helping parents, being happy, being thankful and respecting others.
3. Use a digital device, or pencils, to draw and colour faces that show joy, thankfulness and peace.
4. Each learner reads one good thought aloud.

## Practice
1. Name three good thoughts.
2. What is the difference between a thought and a feeling?
3. What question can you ask to check a thought?

## Summary
• Good thoughts include sharing, helping, happiness, thankfulness and respect.
• Good feelings include joy, peace, love and thankfulness.
• You can notice a wrong thought and replace it with a kind one.

### Answers to practice
1. Any three: sharing with others, helping parents, being happy, being thankful, respecting others.
2. A thought is an idea in the mind. A feeling is what you experience inside, such as joy or sadness.
3. Will this help someone? Is this true? Is this kind?

PAGE 3: Lesson 2: Why it is good to be joyful

LESSON 2: WHY IT IS GOOD TO BE JOYFUL
=====================================

## What you will learn
• Explain the importance of being joyful.
• Recite Philippians 4:4.

Curriculum outcomes: b) explain the importance of being joyful

## Introduction
A joyful learner is not a learner who never has problems. Joy is a glad heart that still trusts God. Philippians 4:4 tells Christians to rejoice in the Lord always.

## Notes
Joy is a deep gladness. It is stronger than a short laugh. You can be joyful when you are thankful, even on a hard day, because joy rests on God and not only on what is happening.

### Philippians 4:4
Philippians 4:4 says, "Rejoice in the Lord always. I will say it again: Rejoice!" Paul repeats the command so that readers will not forget it. Rejoice means to be glad. In the Lord means the gladness comes from knowing God, not only from getting what you want.

Write the verse on a flash card. Read it in the morning. Recite it until you can say it without looking.

### Why joy is important
- Joy shows that you trust God.
- A joyful person is kinder to family and classmates.
- Joy helps you keep going when work is hard.
- Thankfulness and joy belong together. When you count gifts from God, joy grows.
- Joy can spread. A song of rejoicing can lift a whole class.

Being joyful does not mean pretending. If you are hurt, you may tell a trusted adult. Joy and honesty can live in the same heart. You tell the truth about the hurt, and you still rejoice that God is with you.

Songs about rejoicing in the Lord always help the verse stay in your memory. Sing them at home and in church.

## Key words
• joy — a deep gladness that trusts God
• rejoice — to be glad, especially in the Lord

## Worked examples

### Example 1
Otieno lost a game at break and wants to stay angry all afternoon. How can Philippians 4:4 help him?

Working:
1. The verse says rejoice in the Lord always, not only when you win.
2. He can tell a friend he is disappointed and still choose thankfulness.
3. He can sing or recite the verse instead of spoiling the afternoon.

Answer: He can admit he is disappointed and still rejoice in the Lord, because joy does not depend only on winning.

## Activity: Flash cards for Philippians 4:4
You will need: Flash cards or pieces of manila paper, Pens, Bible
1. Read Philippians 4:4 together.
2. Each learner writes the verse on a flash card.
3. In pairs, recite the verse until both can say it from memory.
4. Say why it is good to be joyful.
5. Sing a song about rejoicing in the Lord always.

## Practice
1. Recite Philippians 4:4.
2. What does rejoice mean?
3. Give two reasons why it is good to be joyful.

## Summary
• Joy is deep gladness that rests on God.
• Philippians 4:4 says to rejoice in the Lord always.
• Joy helps you be kind and keep going, even on a hard day.

### Answers to practice
1. Rejoice in the Lord always. I will say it again: Rejoice!
2. To be glad.
3. Any two: joy shows trust in God; a joyful person is kinder; joy helps you keep going; thankfulness grows joy; joy can spread to others.

PAGE 4: Lesson 3: Coping with anger and sadness

LESSON 3: COPING WITH ANGER AND SADNESS
=======================================

## What you will learn
• List lessons learnt from Ephesians 4:26.
• Apply those lessons when coping with anger or sadness.

Curriculum outcomes: c) list lessons learnt from Ephesians 4:26; d) apply the lessons learnt to cope with emotions in day-to-day life

## Introduction
Everyone feels angry or sad sometimes. A friend may take your seat. You may miss someone at home. The question is not whether the feeling comes. The question is what you do with it.

## Notes
Ephesians 4:26 teaches two lessons. First, if you become angry, do not let the anger lead you into sin. Second, do not stay angry all day. Do not let the sun go down while you are still angry. Anger itself is a feeling. Hitting, insulting, refusing to forgive, or planning revenge turns the feeling into sin.

### Lessons from Ephesians 4:26
- You may feel angry, but you must not sin because of it.
- Settle the matter before the day ends.
- Speak the truth calmly instead of shouting.
- Forgive the person who wronged you.
- Ask God to quiet your heart.

### Coping with anger
Stop. Breathe slowly. Do not raise your hand. Tell the person, "That hurt me," if it is safe to speak. If you cannot settle it alone, tell a parent or teacher. Role-play forgiving: one learner admits a wrong, the other says, "I forgive you." Love grows when we forgive.

### Coping with sadness
Sadness is not a sin. You may cry, sit with a friend, or tell your parent what happened. Pray. Remember Philippians 4:4 and thank God for one good thing. Helping someone else can lift a heavy heart. Do not hide sadness until it becomes bitterness.

### Using the lessons every day
At school, if a classmate bumps you, you can choose words instead of a fight. At home, if you are corrected, you can obey without shouting back. Before you sleep, ask, "Am I still angry with anyone?" If yes, forgive before the day ends. That is Ephesians 4:26 in ordinary life.

## Key words
• cope — to handle a hard feeling in a safe way
• forgive — to let go of the wish to punish someone who wronged you
• wrath — strong anger

## Worked examples

### Example 1
Neema's brother tore her exercise book. She wants to tear his book too. It is almost sunset. What should she do?

Working:
1. Ephesians 4:26 says do not let anger lead you into sin.
2. Tearing his book would be paying back wrong with wrong.
3. She should tell a parent, speak calmly, and forgive before the day ends.

Answer: She should not tear his book. She should report the matter, speak calmly and forgive before sunset.

## Activity: Read Ephesians 4:26 and role-play forgiveness
You will need: Bible, Exercise book
1. Read Ephesians 4:26 and write down the lessons learnt.
2. Share with a partner how you cope with anger or sadness.
3. Role-play forgiving someone who has wronged you.
4. Draw two faces: one angry and one peaceful after forgiveness.
5. Recite Philippians 4:4 from your flash card.

## Practice
1. State two lessons from Ephesians 4:26.
2. Is feeling angry always a sin? Explain.
3. Give one safe way to cope with sadness.
4. Why should you forgive before you sleep?

## Summary
• Ephesians 4:26: do not sin in your anger, and do not stay angry all day.
• Cope with anger by stopping, speaking calmly and forgiving.
• Cope with sadness by telling a trusted person, praying and giving thanks.

### Answers to practice
1. Do not let anger lead you into sin. Do not stay angry all day; settle it before the day ends.
2. No. The feeling of anger is not the sin. Letting anger lead you to hurt others, insult them or refuse to forgive is the sin.
3. Any one: tell a parent or friend, pray, thank God for one good thing, cry honestly, help someone else.
4. Ephesians 4:26 says not to let the sun go down while you are still angry.
pages.quiz:
REVISION QUIZ — 1.2 THOUGHTS AND FEELINGS
========================================

Answer all the questions, then mark yourself on the Answers tab.

1. Which of these is a good thought?
   A. Planning to hide a friend's pencil
   B. Helping parents at home
   C. Laughing at someone's mistake
   D. Wishing harm on a classmate

2. Being thankful and respecting others are examples of:
   A. bad feelings
   B. good thoughts
   C. revenge
   D. sadness

3. What does rejoice mean?
   A. To stay angry
   B. To be glad
   C. To hide your feelings
   D. To copy someone

4. Complete the verse: "Rejoice in the Lord ______."
   A. sometimes
   B. always
   C. never
   D. only on Sunday

5. Why is it good to be joyful?

6. Ephesians 4:26 teaches that when you are angry you should:
   A. let the anger lead you into sin
   B. stay angry until the next week
   C. not sin, and not stay angry all day
   D. hit the person who wronged you

7. Which lesson comes from Ephesians 4:26?

8. A classmate bumps you and you want to hit back. What should you do?
   A. Hit back at once
   B. Stop, speak calmly and forgive
   C. Stay angry all night
   D. Tear the classmate's book

9. Which is a safe way to cope with sadness?
   A. Hide it until you become bitter
   B. Tell a trusted person and pray
   C. Insult everyone around you
   D. Refuse to eat for many days without telling anyone

10. Role-playing forgiveness shows which value?
   A. Love
   B. Pride
   C. Revenge
   D. Fear
pages.answers:
ANSWERS — 1.2 THOUGHTS AND FEELINGS
========================================

1. B. Helping parents at home
   Helping parents is one of the good thoughts named in this sub-strand.

2. B. good thoughts
   Thankfulness and respect are good thoughts that build peace.

3. B. To be glad
   Philippians 4:4 tells Christians to rejoice, which means to be glad in the Lord.

4. B. always
   Philippians 4:4 says, "Rejoice in the Lord always."

5. Any one: joy shows trust in God; it makes you kinder; it helps you keep going; it spreads to other people.
   Joy rests on God and helps people live well together.

6. C. not sin, and not stay angry all day
   The verse warns against sinning in anger and against letting the sun go down on your anger.

7. Do not let anger lead you into sin, and settle the anger before the day ends.
   Those are the two lessons of the verse.

8. B. Stop, speak calmly and forgive
   Coping with anger means refusing to sin and choosing forgiveness.

9. B. Tell a trusted person and pray
   Telling a trusted person and praying are safe ways to cope.

10. A. Love
   Forgiving someone who wronged you is an act of love.
